pages.text: An earthquake sends out two kinds of wave. $(thing)Pressure waves$() push and pull the rock along their path and travel fastest, about 6 km/s in the crust. $(thing)Shear waves$() shake it sideways and travel at about 3.5 km/s. The farther the source, the larger the gap between them: d = Δt·v_p·v_s/(v_p − v_s).
The $(item)Seismograph$() must stand on solid ground. Each finished run times the echoes from below and reports the depth of the nearest ore or cave - within 64 m and three blocks to either side.
